1. Allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
2. Petitioners seek quashing of FIR No. 307/2022 of PS Samaypur Badli for offence under Section 498A/406/34 IPC.
The quashing is sought on the ground that petitioners have compromised the disputes with the complainant de facto (respondent no.2).
3. None appears for petitioners.
4. Learned APP for State and respondent no.2 in person (accompanied with counsel) accept notice.
5. In view of seriousness of allegations of sexual misconduct in the FIR, This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 08/07/2025 at 22:29:38 respondent no.2 is directed to file her affidavit as to whether the same are truthful.
The affidavit is necessary in order to ascertain the further proceedings.
In case the allegations are truthful according to respondent no.2, the quashing, if allowable, should be subject to certain terms.
On the other hand, if the allegations are not truthful according to respondent no.2, the consequences of lodging a false complaint must follow.
Every false complaint creates an artefact of suspicion against complaints of even genuine victims.

It is for these reasons that respondent no.2 is directed to file her Yogesh Aggarwal And Ors vs State (Nct Of Delhi) And Anr on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/93960816/

sentences.text: At this stage, it is disclosed by learned counsel for respondent no.2 that pertaining to the sexual misconduct alleged in the present FIR, one more FIR was registered as FIR No. 222/2022 of PS Samaypur Badli and the said FIR is also a subject matter of another quashing petition, listed today itself before the bench of HMJ Ravinder Dudeja.
That being so, as requested by learned counsel for respondent no.2, list this matter before HMJ Ravinder Dudeja subject to orders of learned Judge In-charge (Criminal Side) on 10.07.2025.
GIRISH KATHPALIA, J JULY 8, 2025/DR
